newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Isolated clashes break out in West Bank.
newsitem.headline: Isolated clashes break out in West Bank.

text.p: Palestinians and Israeli soldiers clashed for a fourth straight day in the West Bank on Saturday but most of the area remained quiet, witnesses said.

Despite intensive U.S. efforts to arrange talks between Israeli and Palestinian leaders to end the violence which has killed 68 people since Wednesday, a Palestinian official said President Yasser Arafat would not be meeting Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday.
Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak has offered to host the meeting in Cairo.
Three Palestinians were lightly injured in a clash in the village of Jabal al-Mukaber, near East Jerusalem, Palestinians said.

In another confrontation, Israeli soldiers fired teargas and rubber bullets at Palestinians who burned tyres and blocked roads in the villages of Halhoul and Beit Umar near the West Bank city of Hebron but no one was injured.

Palestinians in the West Bank observed a general strike to mourn the 54 victims killed in clashes with Israeli troops. Israeli and Palestinian security forces remained on high alert in the West Bank, Gaza Strip and Jerusalem.

Other areas were quiet and shops in most parts of the West Bank remained shut on Saturday as Palestinian police barred civilians from reaching Israeli army positions around PLO-ruled towns in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
Palestinian students returned to school in some cities in the West Bank and Gaza in a sign of easing tension in the self-rule areas.

Israelis and Palestinians blamed each other for the fatal clashes triggered by Israel's opening of an archaeological tunnel near Jerusalem's al-Aqsa mosque, Islam's third holiest shrine. Fourteen Israeli soldier have been killed in the unrest.

"This ugly crime carried out by the Israeli troops reflects a predetermined plot that was being implemented," the PLO executive committee and Palestinian cabinet said in a statement issued early on Saturday.
"The PLO appeals to the world to press Israel to stop implementing its dangerous plot against Islamic and Christian holy sites," it said.
Netanyahu accused Arafat of instigating the violence and demanded he intervene immediately to stop it.
"He must personally intervene and stop the incitement..." Netanyahu said on Friday.
Israeli and Palestinian security officials met on Friday to discuss ways of calming the situation, said Jibril Rajoub, the Palestinian security chief in the West Bank.
Despite similiar pledges on Thursday, gun battles and stone-throwing raged across the West Bank, Gaza Strip and Arab East Jerusalem on Friday.
